title: Keystone performance hub prototype: per-model & per-route analytics canvas
creator: Amira Patel
description: Design and prototype a unified Performance Hub canvas that surfaces per-model and per-route telemetry (latency percentile bands, throughput, token-level cost, cache hit rates) with rapid rollup filtering, inline comparisons, and lightweight drilldowns. This ticket covers the exploratory wireframes, hi-fi prototype for stakeholder review, and a spec for three chart families (latency waterfall, throughput lane, token-cost sankey) plus interaction patterns for canary rollouts and model variant fallbacks.
comments: 2025-02-28 — Kickoff: scoped to two primary personas: SRE engineer (ops-first) and PM/feature owner (cost/quality). Agreed success metrics: reduce mean time to insight for latency regressions from 45m to <15m; expose token-unit cost deltas per-rollout.

2025-03-01 — Early wireframes uploaded: figma://redwood/keystone-v1 (link below). Focus on a central canvas with left-hand route picker, top model selector, and an adaptive midline that converts between summary and deep-dive modes.

2025-03-02 — Eng review (Diego Ramos): suggested replacing absolute token-cost numbers with normalized cost-per-1k-tokens to avoid confusion across routes with different tokenization. Also requested inclusion of KV cache hit rate as a first-class metric.
2025-03-03 — PM feedback (Nora Singh): add a toggle for time-aligned compare (compare previous deploy vs current canary) and quick-export to CSV for finance teams.

2025-03-04 — Design critique (Platform Design): accessibility notes — ensure color-blind safe palettes for percentile bands and provide hovers with textual summaries for each quantile. Also flagged potential visual noise in token-cost sankey if too many nodes are shown.

2025-03-05 — Updated prototype v0.2 pushed: changed cost normalization, added cache-hit mini-sparkline on route list, and added a compact waterfall mode optimized for density on small screens. Ready for PM/Eng signoff.
decisions: Display latency as stacked percentile bands (p50, p90, p99) with an option to overlay token watermarks when sequence lengths vary.
Normalize cost as cost-per-1k-tokens and show both absolute and delta views to avoid misinterpretation by finance stakeholders.
Introduce a compact waterfall display for dense overviews; deep-dive panel will show microtraces for a selected time window.
Cache hit rate is promoted to a primary metric on per-route rows to reflect impact on token-unit cost and tail latency.
Comparisons will be time-aligned and support deploying-tag comparisons (canary vs baseline) with automatic highlight of metrics that exceed configured thresholds.
Use a neutral, colorblind-safe palette and rely on shape/line thickness for additional dimension signaling to support accessibility.
next_steps: Finalize hi-fi prototype for stakeholder demo (owner: Lena) — target 2025-03-09.
Work with Eng (Diego) to map telemetry endpoints and confirm sample sizes needed for p99 stability — blocker until 2025-03-06.
Create acceptance checklist for QA: hover states, keyboard navigation, CSV export consistency, plotting at 1m/5m/1h rollups.
Coordinate a 30min walkthrough with Finance to validate cost normalization and CSV schema.
Prepare handoff artifact: component spec sheet (charts, axes, interactions) and token-budget UI patterns for runtime-1.20 release.
Schedule design signoff meeting (calendar invite) and attach final screens to the Console design system library.
Add a small A/B test to measure whether compact waterfall reduces time-to-insight vs classic waterfall (metrics & duration to be defined by Eng/PM).
